description: The plot illustrates how accuracy (ACC) varies with co-occurrence number for six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale, spanning from about 1 to about 10³ (major ticks shown at 0, 10¹, 10², and 10³). The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale, ranging roughly from 40% to 66%, with labeled ticks at 45, 50, 55, 60, and 65. The Base series is a black solid line with circular markers, increasing from about 39% at the smallest co-occurrence value to about 42% near 10¹, then to about 44% around 10², and staying near 44% at the largest co-occurrence value. FT is a blue solid line with downward-triangle markers, rising from about 40% to about 43% (near 10¹), then to about 46% (near 10²), and ending around 48% at the largest x value. IKE is a red solid line with upward-triangle markers, moving from about 43% at the smallest x to about 45% near 10¹, then about 46–47% near 10², and ending around 49–50%. MEND is a brown solid line with diamond markers, increasing from about 44–45% to about 49% near 10¹, then to about 54% near 10², and ending around 56–57%. MEMIT is a purple solid line with pentagon markers, rising from about 44% to about 51% near 10¹, then to about 53% near 10², and ending around 55%. ROME is a green solid line with square markers, increasing from about 51% at the smallest x to about 57% near 10¹, then to about 62–63% near 10², and ending around 66%.
